_comment: HUMAN listening verdicts. Hand-written, never generated -- no tool may rewrite this file, because the whole value of it is that a person said so. abpage.py reads it and shows the verdict on each tune's page and in the index. Key by the staged tune name (the .sid stem).
_staleness: `sng_sha256` is the sha256 of the .sng the listener approved, and it is what decides whether the verdict still holds -- NOT `version`. Keying on the version was the first design and it was wrong: v0.5.370 and v0.5.371 changed only abpage.py, which cannot alter one byte of audio, and both invalidated ACE_II's approval. That is this repo's own passthrough-guard lesson wearing different clothes -- a staleness check must key on the thing that would make the verdict lie (the conversion changing), never on a proxy that moves more often (any version bump). `version` is kept as provenance only, so a reader knows when the listening happened.

ACE_II.note: Approved after the wave-program slide travel, the filter cutoff step, the bit-6 rest envelope silence and the vibrato depth fix. The depth change itself was not audible to the listener -- this signs off the tune as it stands, not that change in isolation.

Action_Biker.note: RE-APPROVED after --silent-park, on audio re-staged at this sha. THE KNOWN DEFECT THE PREVIOUS VERDICT CARRIED IS NOW CLOSED, which is the reason this entry was rewritten rather than left standing: that sign-off (0.5.375, sha 1bc6f4fa) said explicitly that it covered how the tune SOUNDS and not how long it runs, because our conversion looped forever where the original stops. Measured 180 s both sides: the original's last attack is at 59.54 s and ours now ends at 59.68 s, with 291 attacks against the original's 291 -- identical, where before the park ours made 856 and looped every 61.44 s. Hubbard's $FE means 'tune ended' and a Goattracker orderlist still cannot say it; the tune is parked on a silent pattern instead, which ends it in every way a listener can hear. The +-5 second rule in CLAUDE.md is satisfied for this file at +0.14 s. Nothing else about the tune changed -- the orderlist gained one position and the pattern table one silent pattern, and the per-loop note counts were already right.

5_Title_Tunes.note:
Approved after the pulse phase. The listener's report was that voice 1 sounded wrong from about 43 s and that the instruments did not sound like the original -- the notes were already exact there (melody/seq/pitch/onset 100%), so it was never the music. Three things were fixed between the complaint and this sign-off, in the order they were found. The GATE was 50%: HARD_RESTART_FRAMES=2 against a player that releases for 4, now hard_restart_frames 4 with max_hard_restart, 75%. NOTE LENGTHS were wrong on every note: `hold` read 0.0000 because our $09 testbit frame splits each note's waveform run, now real_firstwave_instruments [1,2,3,5,6,8] for wave 90->99% and hold 0->86% (instrument 7 excluded -- with it, melody collapses to 0.9475). And the DUTY CYCLE, which is what the 43 s complaint actually was: the player's pulse accumulator free-runs and is never reseeded, so its notes open all over the band while ours opened every note on the record's width -- pspan 0.47x, pphase 0.25x. --pulse-phase gives each note a CMD_SETPULSEPTR naming the accumulator's own phase; pspan 1.05x, pphase 1.00x, and instrument 5's onset list now matches the original's exactly.

APPROVED WITH THREE KNOWN, MEASURED LIMITS, recorded so this sign-off is not read as covering them. `gate` cannot exceed 75% on this file: the original gates off 4 calls before the next note and the row is 4 calls, and gplay.c:334's counter==gatetimer IS the note-fetch trigger -- forcing 4 was tested and gives 3 attacks out of 938. `adsr` 58% is half that same gate deficit restated and half AD on frames where both sides are gated off, which is inaudible and self-restoring. `pitch` 98% (from 100%) is the price of the firstwave set, bought for 9 points of wave and 86 of hold with melody and sequence unmoved.
